column1: # Game profile of Hollow Knight (Switch, update 1.5.12620 = v589824). Plays on the Mac

# Unity 6000.0.61f1 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 20.5.21, NVN; subsdk0 is the movie module, which plays the opening cinematic (MP4). The shaders are Shader objects in data.unity3d and the UnityFS bundles of StreamingAssets, read by unityfs.py.
# Docked (1920x1080; present interval 2 while a cinematic plays) with the 2D pad layout: B jumps, Y attacks

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)

# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true. As with Silksong's Unity 6, main never sets a heap and the log shows no StandardAllocator: Unity maps its memory itself in the alias region.

# The 5 GB block of the other Unity games with virtual address memory (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region). The SDK-wide node area cut applies (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py MATCH_CUTS).

# Measured on the Mac in King's Pass: the alias region's high-water mark +1.75 GB, 1.25 GB mapped. The pool is the hardware's (3.2 GB): Unity only reads it through QueryMemoryInfo, and nothing maps against it
# the game sets near = 0 at startup (log: "depth mode near=0"): the pipeline bases made before the game runs take the main0_z vertex entries
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader and ComputeShader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles
